Present effectively both in oral and written formats, with a clear rationale and logical organization.
Understand and apply the fundamental principles of academic integrity, including appropriate use of copyright and intellectual property related to scientific literature.

LIFS 5001.title: Responsible Conduct of Biomedical and Biotechnology Research
LIFS 5001.description: This course will present some of the most common ethical issues encountered in biomedical research and biotechnology. Students will engage in active discussion to provide deeper understanding of each issue. The objective of this course is to raise awareness of the ethical issues around biomedical/bioengineering research, and encourage critical and responsible consideration of research conduct. Topics covered will fall into three categories: 1) Research integrity, 2) Applied ethics in biological research and biotechnology, and 3) Contemporary ethical issues arisen from emerging biotechnologies. Graded P or F.
cilos: Describe potential important ethical issues that biomedical researchers may face in their careers.
When presented with a case or specific scenario, identify the explicit or potential ethical issues, arguments, and perspectives arising from the case or scenario.
Critically analyze and evaluate ethical issues revolving around contemporary biomedical/life science research in a contextual manner, and form and justify their own position on these ethical issues.
Recall and describe key principles, policies, and regulations relevant to the ethical and responsible conduct of research (e.g. Nuremberg Code).
Identify administrative or other resources on campus that researchers can access to seek assistance with ethical issues they may be facing.
Communicate and present ideas to others in a clear and critical manner about complex issues, both in presentation and written format.
Engage in open and thoughtful discussions with peers on complex ethical issues.

LIFS 5070.title: Workshops in Biosciences
LIFS 5070.description: Laboratory exercises, including recombinant DNA technology, protein purification, microscopy, tissue culture and other technologies currently in use.
cilos: Acquire knowledge of experimental technologies.
Analyze and interpret numerical data and demonstrate proficiency in selected modern technology for life science .
Formulate  questioning in a practical settings.

LIFS 5111.title: Advanced Topics in Structural Biology
LIFS 5111.description: This postgraduate course offers an in-depth exploration of structural biology for students interested in understanding the intricate relationship between molecular structure and biological function. Students will engage with fundamental concepts, advanced techniques, and current research topics in the field. In addition to theoretical knowledge, the course emphasizes practical skills through hands-on sessions with software programs like Chimera and PyMOL. Students will learn how to visualize molecular structures and create publication-quality figures and videos, essential tools for effective scientific communication.
cilos: Have a comprehensive understanding of structural biology principles and their applications in research for advanced studies and professional opportunities in the field.
Read structural biology papers with a critical eye.
Present structural biology results in publication quality.

LIFS 5260.title: Biochemical and Molecular Basis of Diseases
LIFS 5260.description: Advanced topics on the biochemical basis of human diseases, molecular medicine and structure based drug design; an oral presentation and a written essay on a specific topic are required.
cilos: Recognize the molecular mechanism underling certain human diseases.
Apply knowledge from modern biomedical sciences to evaluate current treatments and envision potential future treatments.

LIFS 5310.title: Biostatistics: Theory and Application in Life Science Research
LIFS 5310.description: Statistical analysis has become an essential component in research for testing hypothesis and designing experiments. This course is tailored to postgraduate students in Life Science. We will introduce common methodologies used in research, such as ANOVA, linear regression, nonparametric methods, and bootstrapping. The students will also gain practical skills of using R for analysis.
cilos: Translate scientific questions into appropriate statistical models and hypothesis.
Perform statistical analysis using R given experimental data.
Interpret analysis results in the scientific context.
Determine the power of hypothesis testing and use it to guide experimental design.
Develop statistical thinking and describe the basic theories, potential pitfalls, and limitations of main methods.

LIFS 5710.title: Cellular Regulation
LIFS 5710.description: Molecular basis of cellular regulation. Cellular signal transduction cascades.
cilos: Identify the latest concepts in selected cellular processes and the basic mechanisms underlying these processes.
Recognize how new discoveries can improve ways to treat different diseases.
Apply the knowledge learnt in the course to problem solving in their own research.

LIFS 6000.title: Special Topics in Life Science
LIFS 6000.description: This course includes selected topics of current interest in Life Science which are not covered by existing courses. Credit to be determined on case by case basis based on workload. May be repeated for credit, if different topics are covered. Enrollment may require approval of the course instructor.
cilos: Identify the fundamental knowledge of the selected topics of current interest which may not be covered by existing courses.

LIFS 6111.title: Life Science Postgraduate Student Seminar
LIFS 6111.description: Advanced seminar series presented by postgraduate students on their research topics in biological sciences offered in Fall/Spring Terms. This course may be repeated for credit. Graded PP, P or F.
cilos: Prepare effectively abstracts announcing a scientific presentation.
Give formal research seminars of their own research topic in an organized and rational manner.
Develop efficient presentation and communication skills.
Identify the latest development in different research areas of Life Science.
Critically analyze data on other research presentations and provide constructive suggestion to speakers.

LIFS 6112.title: Current Topics in Neuroscience
LIFS 6112.description: This course will expose postgraduate students to selected current topics in Neuroscience. This course may be repeated for credits. Graded P or F.
cilos: Describe the current research findings in the area of neuroscience.
Evaluate and analyze information relevant to neuroscience systematically.
Exchange research information/ideas, communicate and explain information/ideas in the area of neuroscience.

Present research and scientific topics in an organized and rational manner, effectively use data and scientific principles to support rational conclusions and defend them in the discussion part of the presentation.

LIFS 6113.title: Current Topics in Biochemistry and Biophysics
LIFS 6113.description: This course will expose postgraduate students to selected current topics in Biochemistry and Biophysics. This course may be repeated for credits. Graded P or F.
cilos: Describe the current research findings in the area of Biochemistry and Biophysics.
Evaluate and analyze information relevant to Biochemistry and Biophysics systematically.
Exchange research information/ideas, communicate and explain information/ideas in the area of Biochemistry and Biophysics.

Present research and scientific topics in an organized and rational manner, effectively use data and scientific principles to support rational conclusions and defend them in the discussion part of the presentation.

LIFS 6114.title: Current Topics in Biotechnology and Traditional Chinese Medicine
LIFS 6114.description: This course will expose postgraduate students to selected current topics in Biotechnology and Traditional Chinese Medicine. This course may be repeated for credits. Graded P or F.
cilos: Describe the current research findings in the area of Biotechnology and Traditional Chinese Medicine.
Evaluate and analyze information relevant to Biotechnology and Traditional Chinese Medicine systematically.
Exchange research information/ideas, communicate and explain information/ideas in the area of Biotechnology and Traditional Chinese Medicine.

Present research and scientific topics in an organized and rational manner, effectively use data and scientific principles to support rational conclusions and defend them in the discussion part of the presentation.

LIFS 6115.title: Current Topics in Development and Systems Biology
LIFS 6115.description: This course will expose postgraduate students to selected current topics in Development and Systems Biology. This course may be repeated for credits. Graded P or F.
cilos: Describe the current research findings in the area of Development and Systems Biology.
Evaluate and analyze information relevant to Development and Systems Biology systematically.
Exchange research information/ideas, communicate and explain information/ideas in the area of Development and Systems Biology.

Present research and scientific topics in an organized and rational manner, effectively use data and scientific principles to support rational conclusions and defend them in the discussion part of the presentation.

LIFS 6116.title: Current Topics in Genomics and Bioinformatics
LIFS 6116.description: This course will expose postgraduate students to selected current topics in Genomics and Bioinformatics. This course may be repeated for credits. Graded P or F.
cilos: Describe the current research findings in the area of Genomics and Bioinformatics.
Evaluate and analyze information relevant to Genomics and Bioinformatics systematically.
Exchange research information/ideas, communicate and explain information/ideas in the area of Genomics and Bioinformatics.

Present research and scientific topics in an organized and rational manner, effectively use data and scientific principles to support rational conclusions and defend them in the discussion part of the presentation.

LIFS 6117.title: Current Topics in Cell Biology
LIFS 6117.description: This course will expose postgraduate students to selected current topics in Cell Biology. This course may be repeated for credits. Graded P or F.
cilos: Describe the current research findings in the area of Cell Biology.
Evaluate and analyze information relevant to Cell Biology systematically.
Exchange research information/ideas, communicate and explain information/ideas in the area of Cell Biology.

Present research and scientific topics in an organized and rational manner, effectively use data and scientific principles to support rational conclusions and defend them in the discussion part of the presentation.

LIFS 6170.title: Special Topics in Molecular, Cell and Developmental Biology
LIFS 6170.description: Recent advances in molecular, cell and developmental biology will be presented and discussed in lectures and tutorials.
cilos: Be acquainted with historical and current research in each of the topic areas.
Develop the ability to assess scientific literature by reading research article.
Develop the ability to review and present scientific literature through oral presentations.

LIFS 6410.title: Seminar Enrichment Course
LIFS 6410.description: Study on selected current topics in life science through attending seminars in LIFS seminar series. Students can repeat the course for credits. Graded PP, P or F.
cilos: Broaden the interests and knowledge of postgraduate students by inviting mostly external speakers to discuss current topics at the frontiers of biological sciences.
Enhance students’ communication and social skills via interacting with the well-known speakers through questions during the seminars and casual setting (such as student luncheons and reception).

LIFS 6420.title: Project Research
LIFS 6420.description: Project research in one of the life science research laboratories under the supervision of a faculty member. Graded P or F. (for Visiting Internship Postgraduate student)
cilos: Design and plan an experimental approach to test a specific hypothesis, to carry out research and to organize research tasks to meet a deadline.
Implement the planned experimental procedures under the guidance of senior laboratory personnel.
Communicate in a clear and organized manner an evaluation of a project, scientific interpretation of the data and conclusions reached.
Apply experience and technical ability to undertake future research on Life Science.

LIFS 6660.title: Molecular Medicine
LIFS 6660.description: This joint course offered under the HKU-CUHK-HKUST Centre for Advanced Study will give an introduction to basic concepts as well as modern techniques and technologies in Molecular Medicine. Cancer as well as neurodegenerative diseases will be used as disease models in most of the examples covered in the course. Classes will be held in the campus of the university concerned for that part of the course offered.
cilos: Obtain basic knowledge of chromosomal abnormalities in tumour cells, methods for detection and their clinical significance.
Discuss the genetic basis of cancer and implications for clinical diagnosis, prognostication and disease monitoring.
Special topics in neuroscience/cancer biology: to focus on neuronal signaling and neurodegenerative diseases, and cell cycle control.
Cell signaling: to discuss the concept and techniques used in signal transduction study and its connection with cancer.
To obtain basic knowledge in molecular diagnostics.
To obtain basic concepts on the design of molecular medicine studies, including statistical considerations.
To obtain basic knowledge on high throughput molecular technologies, including those used in proteomics and the mass spectrometric analysis of nucleic acids.

LIFS 6800.title: Frontiers in Nucleic Acid Research
LIFS 6800.description: This course will cover the biogenesis and function of non-coding RNAs, drawn from molecular, biochemical and cell biological studies. Dysfunction of non-coding RNA in disease and the application of non-coding RNA as research tools will be discussed.
cilos: Explain how diverse classes of non-coding RNA were discovered and characterized.
Explain how biological processes can be regulated by non-coding RNA.
Critically assess the scientific literature in writing.
Critically review and present scientific literature in oral presentations.
Develop experiments concerning the use or characterization of non-coding RNA in biological studies.

LIFS 6990.title: MPhil Thesis Research
LIFS 6990.description: Master's thesis research supervised by a faculty member. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.
cilos: Design, develop and conduct original research in Life Science.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.

LIFS 7990.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
LIFS 7990.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.
cilos: Design, develop and conduct original research in Life Science.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.
